item.title: New Amazon Data Center Stokes Worry It Would Be the Most Polluting Power Plant in the U.S.
item.author: Hiroko Tabuchi
item.content:encoded: The tech giant is investing in the natural-gas-burning power plant as part of a huge data center in Texas, even as it pledges to honor climate commitments.

item.title: Singapore to Ensure AI Helps Workers Worried About Jobs, PM Says
item.author: Shamim Adam and Philip J. Heijmans
item.content:encoded: Singapore is benefitting from the rapid growth of artificial intelligence and the government is making use of the technology to ensure higher productivity and better jobs for workers who are worried about their livelihoods, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said.

item.title: Data Center Firm Switch to File Confidentially for IPO
item.author: Bailey Lipschultz
item.content:encoded: Switch Inc. filed confidentially for a US IPO, according to people familiar with the matter, joining its data center peers in tapping demand for exposure to the artificial intelligence theme.

item.title: PGA Tour CEO Exclusive and David Kelly Talks Investing | Bloomberg Money 8/7/2026
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg Money takes the pulse of your financial life, powered by the reporting of our global newsroom. Today's guests: Meredith Whitney Advisory Group CEO Meredith Whitney, JPMorgan Asset Management Chief Global Strategist David Kelly, and PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Spelman President on Federal Funding, AI Popularity
item.content:encoded: Spelman College President, Dr. Ayanna Howard, sits down with Romaine Bostick to discuss the impact of federal funding rollbacks for HBCUs, and the impact of AI on college graduates. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Akamai CEO on Earnings, Cloud Industry, New Investment
item.content:encoded: Akamai's shares declined following the release of its second-quarter earnings report, despite the company beating earnings estimates. Tom Leighton, Co-Founder and CEO of Akamai, joined the program to discuss the company's performance and recent developments. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: SoftBank-Backed 3D Printer Maker Formlabs Said to Weigh IPO
item.author: Bailey Lipschultz
item.content:encoded: Formlabs, a maker of 3D printers, is in early talks with potential advisers for an initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Gen CEO on Earnings, New Cybersecurity Attack Tracker
item.content:encoded: Gen Digital's shares are reaching their highest levels in nearly a year following an upward revision of its earnings forecast. Vincent Pilette, President and CEO of Gen Digital, expressed strong confidence in sustaining double-digit growth over the coming quarters, driven by increased demand for cybersecurity solutions amid growing concerns related to AI and agentic technologies. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: JPMorgan Boosts Tech Bond Sales Outlook as AI Debt Binge Expands
item.author: Charlotte Plaskwa
item.content:encoded: JPMorgan Chase & Co. sees bond sales from technology-related firms exceeding half a trillion dollars this year, as hyperscalers’ appetite to deploy capital for the artificial intelligence buildout shows no sign of abating despite growing investor fatigue.

item.title: US Sanctions Iranian Crypto Exchanges As Talks Continue
item.author: Magdalena Del Valle
item.content:encoded: The US ramped up economic pressure on Iran with more sanctions targeting digital asset exchanges and networks connected to the country’s shadow-banking system, as Washington seeks leverage amid ongoing negotiations over the war.

item.title: Jobs Shock Sends Stocks Higher | Open Interest 8/7/2026
item.content:encoded: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Stocks rise after data showed US employers unexpectedly cut jobs in July. Meanwhile, oil wavers as prospects for a lasting agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz remain elusive. National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett, BlackRock’s Rick Rieder and Julia Coronado of MacroPolicy Perspectives react to the surprising jobs report and what it means for the economy and Fed policy. Tanger CEO Stephen Yalof offers a read on the consumer. Plus, Ethan Allen Chairman & CEO Farooq Kathwari responds to an activist campaign seeking to replace the company’s entire board. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: OpenAI Pauses Some Work on New Astra Model on Cyber Concerns
item.author: Seth Fiegerman
item.content:encoded: OpenAI is pausing some internal work around one of its upcoming artificial intelligence models to implement stricter safeguards after the system was found to be significantly more adept at cybersecurity tasks.

item.title: The White House’s Secret A.I. Rules + The State of Model Alignment With METR’s Chris Painter + The Final Hot Mess Express
item.author: Kevin Roose, Casey Newton, Rachel Cohn, Whitney Jones, Vjeran Pavic, Katie McMurran, Dan Powell, Elisheba Ittoop, Rowan Niemisto and Alyssa Moxley
item.content:encoded: A few details from the White House’s A.I. plan have leaked to the news media, but the administration has officially communicated almost nothing.

item.title: SK Hynix Said to Mull Options for $3 Billion Chongqing Plant
item.author: Pei Li and Dong Cao
item.content:encoded: South Korea’s SK Hynix Inc. is considering options for its Chongqing, China-based facility, including bringing in an investor to help accelerate growth, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

item.title: Meta Ordered to Pay $567 Million Fine by New Mexico Judge
item.author: Eli Tan
item.content:encoded: The penalty, imposed by a state judge, is on top of a $375 million fine ordered by a jury that found Meta misled users about the safety of its platforms.

item.title: China’s Unitree Prices IPO in Bet Investors Are Ready for Humanoid Robots
item.author: Steve Lohr and Xinyun Wu
item.content:encoded: Unitree Robotics wants to raise about $900 million in an I.P.O. that tests market interest in humanoid robots, a technology that wows but has yet to prove its viability.

item.title: French Streamers Convicted in Case Related to Kick Livestream Death
item.author: Jonathan Wolfe
item.content:encoded: The two men, users of the platform Kick, received suspended sentences and fines.

item.title: Follow the Markets and Track Stocks With These Free Apps
item.author: J. D. Biersdorfer
item.content:encoded: Google Finance and Apple’s Stocks app have added new features over the years to make them more useful for tracking the markets and your investments.

item.title: CAIS CEO Talks New Funding Round, AI’s Fintech Impact
item.content:encoded: Matt Brown, Founder, Chairman, and CEO of CAIS, discussed the company's recent $170 million Series D funding round led by Vista and supported by AllianzBernstein, Blue Owl, and Carlyle, which values the alternative asset investment platform at over $2 billion—more than double its previous valuation. Brown highlighted CAIS's 37% organic growth and explained that the new capital will be used to pursue strategic mergers and acquisitions in response to ongoing fintech industry consolidation, enhance AI capabilities to improve the platform's user experience for advisers and asset managers, and provide liquidity to long-term shareholders through an institutional tender offer facilitated by Nasdaq Private Markets. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: F.C.C. Removes Limit on Broadcast TV Ownership
item.author: Cecilia Kang
item.content:encoded: The move lifts a rule that said a single television-station owner could not reach more than 39 percent of U.S. households.

item.title: TikTok Lays Off 250 Employees in Office That Includes Content Moderation
item.author: Emmett Lindner
item.content:encoded: TikTok did not give a detailed reason for the layoffs, which will shutter its Nashville office.

item.title: How China’s A.I. Is Surging Across Africa
item.author: Paul Mozur, Adam Satariano and Aaron Krolik
item.content:encoded: In African tech hubs, developers are picking China’s cheap, freely available artificial intelligence models over more powerful U.S. ones.

item.title: Google Names Demis Hassabis to New AI Role in a Leadership Shake-up
item.author: Kate Conger and Cade Metz
item.content:encoded: Minutes after four top researchers said they were leaving, Google said that Demis Hassabis, the Nobel-winning scientist who led the company’s A.I. lab, was stepping into a new job.

item.title: Four Top Google A.I. Researchers Form New Start-Up
item.author: Cade Metz
item.content:encoded: Jeff Dean, who for years was one of Google’s most important executives, is leading the new artificial intelligence company with the backing of Google.

item.title: A SpaceX Rocket Will Soon Crash Into the Moon
item.author: Kenneth Chang
item.content:encoded: The second stage of a Falcon 9 rocket, which sent two private landers to the moon last year, will collide with the moon early Wednesday morning.

item.title: Trump White House Readies AI Framework to Review Security Risks
item.author: David McCabe, Mike Isaac, Kate Conger and Ana Swanson
item.content:encoded: The voluntary review process will cover closed-source artificial intelligence models, but exclude those that publish the underlying code.

item.title: SpaceX, in First Earnings After IPO, Reports Soaring AI Spending
item.author: Ryan Mac
item.content:encoded: Elon Musk’s rocket company said its capital expenditures jumped nearly seven times from a year ago. Revenue also rose.

item.title: White House Whipsaws Silicon Valley (and Itself) Over A.I. Rules
item.author: David McCabe, Mike Isaac, Ana Swanson and Kate Conger
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration has struggled with how to approach “open source” models, which are freely available to download and favored by Chinese companies.

item.title: In Lawsuit, NJ Accuses Amazon of Suppressing Pay for Delivery Drivers
item.author: Karen Weise
item.content:encoded: The state attorney general said in an antitrust lawsuit filed on Tuesday that the company was abusing its market power to keep its delivery costs low.

item.title: Man’s Claim That Brakes Failed on Jaguar Was Scam to Avoid Car Payments, Court Rules
item.author: Victor Mather
item.content:encoded: Nathan Owen called the police, saying he was trapped in a runaway car. A judge determined it was a lie and sentenced him to more than four years in prison.

item.title: SpaceX’s Stock Lockup Is Expiring. Prepare for a Bumpy Ride.
item.author: Ryan Mac
item.content:encoded: On Thursday, employees and other insiders at Elon Musk’s rocket company will be released from their first stock “lockup” and can start selling some of their shares.

item.title: Google Earth Disables A.I. Tool After One Day Over Disinformation Concerns
item.author: Adeel Hassan
item.content:encoded: A new Google Earth tool allowed the creation of A.I. deepfake maps. The company quickly pulled it back after users noted there were no safeguards to prevent content that could be harmful.

item.title: If You Can’t Beat A.I., Outdress It, Tech Firms and Their Swag Say
item.author: Erin Griffith
item.content:encoded: Over the years, tech workers have proudly worn nerdy company-branded gear. But this generation of hot companies is getting fancy with its merch.
